scope.target: Repository-backed design for consistent Python prerequisite diagnostics across supported validator and package entrypoints
constraints: Ask and resolve exactly one owner-decision question at a time.
Explain behavior, compatibility, package, documentation, and test impacts before each decision.
Until D-009 is resolved, preserve Python 3.11 or newer on every retained Python path; do not silently entrench or lower the current runtime contract.
Apply the approved 25-production-CLI boundary in two ordered batches: 12 portable/downstream entrypoints first, then 13 source-only entrypoints.
Fail before repository mutation or validation success claims.
Do not weaken existing validation, package, upgrade, or release gates.
non_goals: Implement before the accumulated design is explicitly approved.
Silently or implicitly install Python or dependencies; an explicit isolated bootstrap remains an owner decision.
Prepare or publish a framework release.

steps: Inventory all candidate Python entrypoints and classify user-facing support evidence.
Map import timing, mutation potential, package projection, documentation, and tests.
Assess fail-closed, host/versioned/provider runtime discovery, explicit installation, OS-native launcher, and canonical script ownership alternatives.
Reconstruct the Python/PyYAML selection history and distinguish repository evidence from inferred engineering motivation.
Inventory current downstream execution modes, applicability behavior, CI wiring, distribution projection, and the absence of a target-owned activation policy.
Trace retry ownership across the aggregate runner, software-development orchestrator, and root execution guidance; define a token-cost-aware retry decision boundary.

Explain the local activation default through team scenarios, target-owned versus developer-local configuration, precedence, CI dependency, and feedback/token tradeoffs before requesting D-010B approval.

Present the complete D-010B through D-010E control chain together, including local selection, CI enforcement, compatibility-safe result semantics, and bounded Agent/CI observation cost, while requesting only one owner decision at a time.

Separate the approved manual target default from developer-local storage, and compare Git config, ignored strict file, environment, OS-user, and runtime-specific transports against pre-Python, packaging, and cross-Agent constraints.
Identify the proposed shared and local setting locations and map exact producer, preserver, consumer, closeout, audit, unaffected-skill, wrapper, contract, and test impacts.
Separate minimum repository workflow contracts from workflow-owner template semantics, and distinguish framework self-test ownership, package projection, activation, and enforcement.
Present one design decision at a time with impact and alternatives.
Record every owner decision in workflow-plan.md.
Produce an approved implementation boundary and validation matrix.
validation: Repository-native path and reference evidence for every in-scope entrypoint
Valid workflow locator and task artifacts
Explicit owner approval before implementation transition
